slides.texte_overlay:
How to think sharper
than most people
Slow down before you decide. Ask "what am I missing?" Most bad decisions come from jumping to the first answer that feels right.
Think in probabilities. Instead of "this will work" say "this has a good chance." It makes you calmer and more accurate about the future.
Look for the second-order effect. Not just "what happens next" but "and then what?" Thinking one step further sets you apart.
Learn from other people's mistakes. Biographies and history are full of lessons you don't have to learn the hard way. History rarely repeats exactly, but it rhymes.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A wider base of knowledge makes every decision clearer.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A wider base of knowledge makes every decision clearer.

slides.texte_overlay: Keep a decision journal. Write why you chose something, then check months later. You'll quickly see where your thinking goes wrong.
Separate facts from feelings. Ask "what do I actually know?" before reacting. Clear thinkers don't let emotions decide for them.
